newsitem.title: USA: US spot gas prices notionally higher with futures.
newsitem.headline: US spot gas prices notionally higher with futures.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices were mostly stronger Wednesday as Gulf cash followed the rising futures market and warmer forecasts in the West attracted more buyers, industry sources said.
"It's (cash) just chasing the contract. No business is being done," one trader said.
Louisiana Gulf prices at the Henry Hub were talked notionally about seven cents higher at $2.14-2.17 per mmBtu, though no physical trades were reported done.
At 1349 EDT, NYMEX's Henry Hub June contract was 3.8 cents higher at $2.18.
In the Midcontinent, prices rose four cents to the mid-to-high $1.90s, with Demarcation quoted mostly in the high-$1.90s for May 1.
Chicago city-gate values were quoted at $2.19-2.22, while Detroit was notionally talked at $2.34-2.39.
In the Northeast, where mild weather persists, New York city-gate prices were mostly steady in the mid-$2.30s to about $2.40.
Appalachian prices for next month were also little changed in the low-to-mid $2.30s.
In west Texas, Permian prices climbed six cents to about $1.90-1.95, while prices at the southern California border rose a similar amount to about $2.06-2.07.
Traders blamed the price uptick on warmer weather in the southernmost part of the Southwest and forecasts for more of the same through the weekend.
According to a Reuter poll, tonight's American Gas Association storage report is expected to show an average build of 10-25 bcf in the week ended April 25.
